title: External tensor filtration over a finite algebra
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $\Lambda=\mathbf F_\ell$, $A$ a commutative Noetherian $\Lambda$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and $B$ a finite-dimensional unital $\Lambda$-algebra, not necessarily commutative. Here finite-dimensional means finitely generated as a $\Lambda$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Write $C=A\otimes_\Lambda B$, with multiplication $(a\otimes b)(a'\otimes b')=aa'\otimes bb'$ and unit $1\otimes1$; tensor products of modules are [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Every finitely generated left $C$-module $M$ admits a finite filtration by $C$-submodules
$$0=M_0\subseteq M_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq M_t=M$$
such that every $M_i/M_{i-1}$ is a direct summand, as a $C$-module, of $N_i\otimes_\Lambda L_i$, for a finitely generated $A$-module $N_i$ and a simple left $B$-module $L_i$. Simple means nonzero with no nonzero proper $B$-submodule. The action is $(a\otimes b)(n\otimes v)=an\otimes bv$. Direct summand means that there are $C$-linear maps from the quotient into the displayed tensor module and back whose composite on the quotient is the identity. The zero module is allowed with the empty filtration.

source.place: Expose XVII, Lemma 7.4.7, pp. 307-308, specialized to n=ell and Lambda=F_ell.

proof.text: Choose $\Lambda$-generators $b_1,\ldots,b_u$ of $B$ and $C$-generators $m_1,\ldots,m_v$ of $M$. Expanding each coefficient into pure tensors shows that the finitely many $(1\otimes b_i)m_j$ generate $M$ as an $A$-module: $(a\otimes b)m_j=a\sum_i\lambda_i(1\otimes b_i)m_j$ when $b=\sum_i\lambda_i b_i$. Every quotient of an $A$-finite module is $A$-finite by taking images of its generators, and every $A$-submodule of such a module is $A$-finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite]. These observations apply throughout to submodules, quotient layers and matrix corners. If $M=0$, use the empty filtration; in particular this handles $A=0$ or $B=0$, since modules are unital.

source.place: Expose XVII, Lemma 7.4.7, first paragraph, p. 307; explicit finite-generation verification.

proof.text: The finite set $\Lambda^u$ surjects onto $B$, so $B$ has finitely many elements. Its set of left ideals is therefore finite, and every descending sequence of left ideals stabilizes. Apply [lem-per-artinian-radical-semisimple-quotient] to $B$: its two-sided Jacobson radical $J$ satisfies $J^h=0$, with $h\geq1$ after increasing the exponent if necessary, and $S=B/J$ is semisimple. For $0\leq r\leq h$ let $F_r=J^rM$, the set of finite sums of $jm$ with $j\in J^r$. It is stable under $B$ because $J^r$ is two-sided and under $A$ because the two actions commute. Thus $M=F_0\supseteq\cdots\supseteq F_h=0$ is a finite $C$-filtration. Its layer $Q_r=F_r/F_{r+1}$ is annihilated by $J$ since $JF_r\subseteq F_{r+1}$. Consequently its commuting $A$- and $B$-actions give an $A\otimes_\Lambda S$-action by $(a\otimes\bar b)q=abq$, independently of the lift $b$.

source.place: Expose XVII, Lemma 7.4.7, first reduction, p. 307; finite radical-power filtration makes the Noetherian-induction reduction explicit.

proof.text: The images of the $b_i$ generate $S$ over $\Lambda$. Apply [lem-per-semisimple-algebra-matrix-division] with $k=\Lambda$ to obtain $S\simeq\prod_{\alpha=1}^s\operatorname{Mat}_{d_\alpha}(D_\alpha)$, where every $d_\alpha>0$ and $D_\alpha$ is finite-dimensional over $\Lambda$. A finite generating set gives a surjection from a finite set $\Lambda^n$ onto each $D_\alpha$, so [lem-per-finite-division-ring-commutative] makes it a finite field $E_\alpha$ with the same ring operations and coefficient embedding. Let $c_\alpha$ be the central factor idempotents of $S$. For each layer $Q_r$, the maps $q\mapsto(c_\alpha q)_\alpha$ and $(q_\alpha)_\alpha\mapsto\sum_\alpha q_\alpha$ identify it with $\bigoplus_\alpha Q_{r,\alpha}$, where $Q_{r,\alpha}=c_\alpha Q_r$: the identities $\sum c_\alpha=1$ and $c_\alpha c_\beta=0$ for $\alpha\ne\beta$ prove the two composites are identities. Each summand is an $A$-finite module by Step 1, with commuting $A$- and $\operatorname{Mat}_{d_\alpha}(E_\alpha)$-actions.

source.place: Expose XVII, Lemma 7.4.7, second reduction, p. 307: product decomposition and finite division rings.

proof.text: Fix a component $Q=Q_{r,\alpha}$ and abbreviate $d=d_\alpha$, $E=E_\alpha$. Write $e_{ij}$ for the matrix units and put $N=e_{11}Q$. The scalar matrices give $N$ an $E$-action commuting with $A$, and $N$ is $A$-finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite]. Define $\phi:N^d\to Q$ by $\phi((n_i))=\sum_i e_{i1}n_i$ and $\psi:Q\to N^d$ by $\psi(q)=(e_{1i}q)_i$. The identities $e_{1j}e_{i1}=\delta_{ij}e_{11}$ and $\sum_i e_{i1}e_{1i}=1$ show $\psi\phi=1$ and $\phi\psi=1$. For a matrix $T=(t_{ij})$, $e_{1i}Tq=\sum_j t_{ij}e_{1j}q$; hence these are inverse $A$-linear maps intertwining the matrix action on $Q$ with its coordinate action on $N^d$. Let $L=E^d$ with the column action of $B\to S\to\operatorname{Mat}_d(E)$. This is a simple $B$-module: for a nonzero vector $v$, choose $v_j\ne0$; the matrices $v_j^{-1}e_{ij}$ send $v$ to every standard basis vector, and further scalar matrices give every vector. The surjective factor map from $B$ therefore leaves no nonzero proper submodule.

source.place: Expose XVII, Lemma 7.4.7, second reduction, p. 307; explicit matrix-unit verification of the Morita reduction.

proof.text: Use only the algebraic first clause of [lem-pur-finite-field-derived-tensor-summand], with $F=\Lambda$ and $B=E$, to choose $e=\sum_{j=1}^a x_j\otimes y_j\in E\otimes_\Lambda E$ satisfying $\sum_jx_jy_j=1$ and $(z\otimes1)e=(1\otimes z)e$ for every $z\in E$. On $N\otimes_\Lambda E$ give $A$ the first-factor action and $E$ the second-factor action. Define $\beta:N\otimes_\Lambda E\to N$ by $\beta(n\otimes z)=zn$, and $\sigma:N\to N\otimes_\Lambda E$ by $\sigma(n)=\sum_jx_jn\otimes y_j$. The balancing relation makes $\beta$ well-defined and $A$-linear, and both maps are additive and $A$-linear because the $E$-action on $N$ commutes with $A$. Applying the linear map $E\otimes_\Lambda E\to N\otimes_\Lambda E$, $x\otimes y\mapsto xn\otimes y$, to the displayed identity gives $\sigma(zn)=z\sigma(n)$ for the second-factor $E$-action. Also $\beta\sigma(n)=\sum_jx_jy_jn=n$. Thus $N$ is a retract of $N\otimes_\Lambda E$ as an $A\otimes_\Lambda E$-module. No sheaf or derived assertion of the cited node is used.

source.place: Expose XVII, Lemma 7.4.7, third reduction, pp. 307-308; explicit separability splitting replaces the descent shorthand. Algebraic idempotent source: Stacks Tag 0C2X, lemma-separable-algebraic-diagonal.

proof.text: Apply $\sigma$ and $\beta$ coordinatewise. Since they are both $E$-linear and $A$-linear, the resulting maps $N^d\to(N\otimes_\Lambda E)^d\to N^d$ commute with every matrix: the $i$th coordinate of either order of composition is the sum over $j$ of the same map applied to $t_{ij}n_j$. Their composite is the identity. There is an $A$- and matrix-linear isomorphism $\theta:(N\otimes_\Lambda E)^d\to N\otimes_\Lambda E^d$, sending a tensor $n\otimes z$ in coordinate $i$ to $n\otimes zv_i$, where $v_i$ is the $i$th standard vector. Its inverse sends $n\otimes(z_i)_i$ to $(n\otimes z_i)_i$. Balancing and the formula for matrix multiplication verify both compositions and equivariance on pure tensors, which generate. Compose these maps with $\psi$ and $\phi$ from Step 4. They exhibit $Q$ as a retract of $N\otimes_\Lambda L$. The other factors of $S$ and $J$ act as zero on both modules, so these maps are $C$-linear after restriction along $C\to A\otimes_\Lambda S$.

source.place: Expose XVII, Lemma 7.4.7, second and third reductions, pp. 307-308; coordinatewise reconstruction of the external tensor retract.

proof.text: For each $r$, order the finitely many summands $Q_{r,\alpha}$ and filter $Q_r$ by their successive partial sums. The quotient of one partial sum by the preceding one is its next component: projection onto that component and inclusion followed by the quotient are inverse maps. Take inverse images of these partial sums under $F_r\to Q_r$; their endpoints are $F_{r+1}$ and $F_r$, and their successive quotients are the same components by the map induced by this surjection. Concatenate these refinements in the order $r=h-1,h-2,\ldots,0$. This gives an increasing finite filtration from $0$ to $M$. Each quotient has the retract of Step 6 with an $A$-finite $N$ and simple $B$-module $L$, exactly with action $(a\otimes b)(n\otimes v)=an\otimes bv$. Zero components may be omitted. If $s=0$, all $Q_r=0$ and the endpoints force $M=0$, already treated in Step 1.

source.place: Expose XVII, Lemma 7.4.7, first two reductions, p. 307; finite refinement and assembly.
